req.title: Reject non-GET on /get
req.statement: The system shall respond with HTTP 405 Method Not Allowed for any non-GET request to /get.

doc.reasoning: The requirement states that /get must accept GET requests (HTTP 200) and reject all non-GET methods with HTTP 405. The route is defined with methods=("GET",), so Flask will automatically return 405 for POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE, HEAD (non-standard), OPTIONS, etc. Tests cover: (1) positive EP — valid GET returns 200 with correct payload keys; (2) negative EP — POST returns exactly 405; (3) boundary DT — all remaining non-GET methods (PUT, PATCH, DELETE) each return exactly 405; (4) NEG — OPTIONS returns 405 (not 200); (5) BVA — HEAD method (boundary of GET family) returns 405. Each assertion uses exact status codes to catch comparison-operator mutations (== vs >=, 405 vs 404, etc.).

preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
actions: Create Flask test client from httpbin.core.app
expected: Response JSON contains keys: url, args, headers, origin
Response JSON does NOT contain keys: form, data, files, json
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_get_method_returns_200_with_expected_payload():
    r = client.get('/get')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    data = r.get_json()
    assert isinstance(data, dict)
    assert 'url' in data
    assert 'args' in data
    assert 'headers' in data
    assert 'origin' in data
    assert 'form' not in data
    assert 'files' not in data
    assert len(data) == 4

def test_put_patch_delete_to_get_endpoint_each_return_405():
    r_put = client.put('/get')
    assert r_put.status_code == 405

    r_patch = client.patch('/get')
    assert r_patch.status_code == 405

tests.name: test_get_returns_200_not_405_exact_boundary
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
GET is the boundary between allowed and disallowed methods
actions: Create Flask test client from httpbin.core.app
Send GET request to /get (the exact allowed method)
Send POST request to /get (one step beyond allowed)
expected: The two status codes are different from each other
trace: BVA: GET is the sole allowed method; POST is the immediate non-allowed boundary
Catches mutations that flip 405 to 200 or vice versa
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_get_returns_200_not_405_exact_boundary():
    r_get = client.get('/get')
    assert r_get.status_code == 200
    assert r_get.status_code != 405

    r_post = client.post('/get')
    assert r_post.status_code == 405
    assert r_post.status_code != 200

    assert r_get.status_code != r_post.status_code
